newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta firms after EU reaches stability pact deal.
newsitem.headline: Peseta firms after EU reaches stability pact deal.

text.p: The peseta firmed slightly against the mark after diplomats said the European Union had reached a deal on a post-monetary union stability pact.
By 1615 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.15/17 against the mark, compared with 84.20/22 seen earlier in the session and 84.22/24 in late trade on Thursday.
"The peseta is following rises in the dollar and Spanish bonds but we're still only talking about a 10-tick range here," one trader said.
Traders said they did not expect the peseta to strengthen much further against the mark.
Diplomats said the European Union had reached a deal on a pact to enforce budget discipline after its planned union is launched in 1999 and that all 15 countries had agreed.
The news sent the spread between Spanish bonds and Bunds to a new low of 110 and bond futures soaring more than one point.
